title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
body:
Motivation: Production customers are seeing wide variance in per-token unit economics due to suboptimal defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, and a lack of vetted quantization profiles for common model families. This PR centralizes autotune defaults, adds a set of validated quantization profiles, and ships the first iteration of the unit-economics (uecon) tooling so teams can measure impact before rollout.

Summary of changes: - Add autotune defaults for dynamic batching thresholds and cache retention to reduce cold-start token cost while preserving tail latency SLOs. - Introduce quantization profile manifests for gpt-like and llama-like families (int8, smoothfp16-ish hybrid profiles) with measured quality/latency tradeoffs. - Instrument deployment and runtime to surface unit-econ metrics per model+route. - New CLI: redwood uecon analyze --profile to run simulated workload sweeps and output cost/latency/QoR matrices. - Small console integration: per-route cost delta preview in rollout flow.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: Linear ENG-4132 linked
- [x] Perf microbenchmarks (see commits)
- [x] Unit + integration tests for autotune default loader
- [x] E2E uecon CLI smoke tests
- [x] Docs updated (console + CLI)

Implementation details: Autotune defaults live under runtime/config/autotune_defaults.yaml and are applied at request router bootstrap. Defaults include target_batch_size_percentiles (50/95), max_queued_ms thresholds, and prefix_kv_ttl_ms heuristics keyed by model_family and typical sequence length buckets. Quantization profiles are declarative YAML manifests under models/quant_profiles/ with metadata fields: model_family, target_hw, estimated_quality_loss_pct, and fallback_profile. The uecon tool runs a lightweight synthetic request generator against a pinned model binary and measures P50/P95 latency, GPU utilization, and token cost with accounting hooks in the runtime. Results are exported as CSV and optionally uploaded to console for visualization.

Testing and results: On internal bench (gpt-13B-like test shard), enabling autotune defaults recovered 18-26% per-token cost savings for chat-heavy traces with <3% quality regression measured by our eval harness. int8 quant profile for the 13B family reduced GPU memory pressure by 38% and per-token compute cost by ~22% with a 1.6% avg quality delta on the prompt set used. See commit performance summaries for detailed tables.

Rollout plan: feature-flag the defaults on staging for two weeks, run uecon sweeps nightly, gate canary rollout by unit-econ thresholds (default: no increase >2% in avg token-level quality and at least 10% cost reduction). Console preview will show expected deltas before enabling.

Related: ENG-4132, ENG-4188, PM-221.

Notes: Some tests flaked on the first CI run due to a non-deterministic mock (fixed in a follow-up commit). Will monitor canary closely after merge.

review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Left a couple of nits on batching_policy.go — please add a small comment explaining the 95th percentile bind and why we cap at 256. Also suggest a unit test for the TTL behavior.
Ava Chen: Thanks — added the comment and a TTL unit test in tests/integration/test_autotune_defaults.py (commit f4e5d6a).
Priya Patel: Can we add a short note in the docs about model family compatibility for each quant profile? A mismatch caused confusion in earlier runs.
Ava Chen: Added compatibility table to docs/guides/cost_optimization.md and the quant profile manifests include a target_hw field.
Liam O'Connor: UEcon CLI looks good; one request — make the CSV columns stable across runs (added suggestion to serializer).
Ava Chen: Stabilized CSV header ordering in tools/uecon/cli.py (commit e7f8a90).
merge_summary: Merged by Priya Patel via squash and merge. Branch cleaned up after merge. Canary rollout feature-flag enabled for staging. See release notes entry added to docs/guides/cost_optimization.md.
release_notes: Added autotune defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching; introduced base quantization profiles (gpt-like, llama-like); shipped first version of unit-economics (uecon) tooling and console cost preview. Rollout via feature-flag. See docs/guides/cost_optimization.md for details.
